### Ideal Diode I-V Characteristics
An ideal diode acts as a short circuit (zero voltage drop) when forward-biased and as an open circuit (infinite resistance) when reverse-biased.

```text
  I (Current)
    ^
    |
    |     Ideal Diode Characteristic
    |      |
    |      | (Short Circuit for V > 0)
    +------|--------> V (Voltage)
    |      /
    |     /
    |    / (Open Circuit for V < 0)
```

### Circuit Analysis:
Given current source = $10\text{ mA}$.
The current divides into two parallel branches: a $2.2\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor in parallel with the Si diode branch, and a $1.2\text{ k}\Omega$ resistor ($R_L$). 
*Assuming the silicon diode is ON ($V_D = 0.7\text{ V}$ or solved using ideal approx based on standard notations):*
Applying node analysis, the total current $I = 10\text{ mA}$.
Let the voltage at the node be $V_O$.
Using Kirchhoff's Current Law (KCL): 
$$\frac{V_O}{2.2\text{ k}\Omega} + \frac{V_O}{1.2\text{ k}\Omega} + I_D = 10\text{ mA}$$ 
With ideal diode approximation ($V_D = 0\text{V}$), $V_O = 0\text{V}$, hence $I_D = 10\text{ mA}$ (all current flows through the diode branch if forward biased).
proTip: Always check whether the diode is assumed ideal or practical (with $0.7\text{V}$ drop) before writing final values.
